metadata.title: Week 7 KP05 U-Net: contraction, expansion and skip connections (guided version)
metadata.description: IDL 2026 Week 7 KP05; reasoning-led-teaching-deck 2.1; English, self-paced reading; manual advance, try before reveal

scene-root.name: Week 7 KP05 U-Net: contraction, expansion and skip connections (guided version)

scene-u01.name: Week 7 KP05 U-Net: contraction, expansion and skip connections (guided version)

p01-hook-title.name: p01-hook-title
p01-hook-title.text: One class for the whole image, or one class for every pixel?

p01-hook-ctx.name: p01-hook-ctx
p01-hook-ctx.text: AlexNet, VGG and Inception all take 'the whole image in, one class out'. If the task is 'which class does each pixel belong to', the output must be as large as the input.

p01-hook-cls-t.name: p01-hook-cls-t
p01-hook-cls-t.text:
One image → one class (e.g. 'cell')
output: $1000$ scores

p01-hook-gt.name: p01-hook-gt
p01-hook-gt.text: Segmentation: one label per pixel (sketch 8×8, blue = cell, grey = background)

p01-hook-q-t.name: p01-hook-q-t
p01-hook-q-t.text:
To do this the output must be as large as the input.
U-Net was designed for this, first used for biomedical image segmentation (the winner of the ISBI electron-microscopy neuronal-structure segmentation challenge).

p02-shape-title.name: p02-shape-title
p02-shape-title.text: Why does the network take the shape of a U?

p02-shape-ctx.name: p02-shape-ctx
p02-shape-ctx.text: The left side shrinks all the way (catching context: what is this region roughly?), the right side enlarges all the way (precise localization: where is the boundary, at which pixel?).

p02-shape-lt-t.name: p02-shape-lt-t
p02-shape-lt-t.text: Contracting path: shrink and add channels; the range seen grows and the context increases.

p02-shape-rt-t.name: p02-shape-rt-t
p02-shape-rt-t.text: Expansive path: enlarge and reduce channels, finding the positions back cell by cell.

p02-shape-sk-t.name: p02-shape-sk-t
p02-shape-sk-t.text: Skip connections: the feature maps of the same level on the left are sent directly to the right (copy and crop), so details do not get blurred during enlargement.

p03-contract-title.name: p03-contract-title
p03-contract-title.text: What three things does each step of the contracting path do?

p03-contract-ctx.name: p03-contract-ctx
p03-contract-ctx.text: Much like VGG of KP03: small-kernel convolutions, $2\times2$ pooling, channels doubled.

p03-contract-o1-t.name: p03-contract-o1-t
p03-contract-o1-t.text: Stride $2$, downsampling, the side is halved.

p03-contract-o2-t.name: p03-contract-o2-t
p03-contract-o2-t.text: Each downsampling doubles the feature channels.

p03-contract-note-t.name: p03-contract-note-t
p03-contract-note-t.text: The source gives no starting channel count; the original uses $64$, going $64,128,256,512,1024$ [Added]. Shrinking space while deepening channels, the range the network sees keeps growing.

p04-tconv-title.name: p04-tconv-title
p04-tconv-title.text: How does a transposed convolution enlarge 2×2 into 4×4?

p04-tconv-ctx.name: p04-tconv-ctx
p04-tconv-ctx.text: The expansive path uses no pooling but a $2\times2$ transposed convolution to enlarge. Each input value is multiplied by the whole kernel and written into its own $2\times2$ block of the output (the example is [Added]).

p04-tconv-r1-t.name: p04-tconv-r1-t
p04-tconv-r1-t.text: Input $1$ times the kernel, written into the upper-left block: $\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$

p04-tconv-r2-t.name: p04-tconv-r2-t
p04-tconv-r2-t.text: Input $2$ times the kernel, written into the upper right: $\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\0&2\end{pmatrix}$

p04-tconv-r4-t.name: p04-tconv-r4-t
p04-tconv-r4-t.text: The side goes from $2$ to $4$, doubling, and the blocks do not overlap. The kernel numbers are learned, so it is not the 'inverse operation' of convolution and does not restore what pooling discarded.

p05-practice-a-title.name: p05-practice-a-title
p05-practice-a-title.text: Your turn: transposed convolution with an all-ones kernel, concatenated channels, side with padding

p05-practice-a-q1-t.name: p05-practice-a-q1-t
p05-practice-a-q1-t.text: What is the output of the $2\times2$ transposed convolution (stride $2$) with input $\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&4\end{pmatrix}$ and kernel $\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$?

p05-practice-a-q2-t.name: p05-practice-a-q2-t
p05-practice-a-q2-t.text: In the first step of the expansive path, a transposed convolution turns $1024$ channels into $512$. How many channels after concatenating the left $512$ channels?

p05-practice-a-q3-t.name: p05-practice-a-q3-t
p05-practice-a-q3-t.text: If all convolutions use padding $1$ and the input is $256$, what is the side after four poolings of the contracting path?

p05-practice-a-a1-t.name: p05-practice-a-a1-t
p05-practice-a-a1-t.text:
Each cell fills its own $2\times2$:
$\begin{pmatrix}1&1&2&2\\1&1&2&2\\3&3&4&4\\3&3&4&4\end{pmatrix}$, which enlarges every cell into $2\times2$.

p05-practice-a-a2-t.name: p05-practice-a-a2-t
p05-practice-a-a2-t.text: $512+512=1024$ channels; the following convolution brings them back to $512$.

p05-practice-a-a3-t.name: p05-practice-a-a3-t
p05-practice-a-a3-t.text: With padding, convolutions do not change the side and only pooling halves it: $256\to128\to64\to32\to16$, side $16$.

p06-skip-title.name: p06-skip-title
p06-skip-title.text: After enlarging, why attach the feature map from the left?

p06-skip-ctx.name: p06-skip-ctx
p06-skip-ctx.text: After enlarging, the expansive path concatenates it along the channels with the feature map of the 'same level' of the contracting path, then does two $3\times3$ convolutions.

p06-skip-left-t.name: p06-skip-left-t
p06-skip-left-t.text: Feature map of the contracting path: keeps detail (where the edges are) but has little context.

p06-skip-up-t.name: p06-skip-up-t
p06-skip-up-t.text: Enlarged feature map: carries context (what this area is) but the edges are blurred.

p06-skip-conv-t.name: p06-skip-conv-t
p06-skip-conv-t.text:
Two $3\times3$ convolutions + ReLU
(using both kinds of information)

p06-skip-mis-t.name: p06-skip-mis-t
p06-skip-mis-t.text: Common error: thinking a transposed convolution can 'restore' what pooling discarded. It only enlarges the size; details must come back from the left through the skip connection.

p07-sizes-down-title.name: p07-sizes-down-title
p07-sizes-down-title.text: Original U-Net without padding: how does the side change?

p07-sizes-down-ctx.name: p07-sizes-down-ctx
p07-sizes-down-ctx.text: Each $3\times3$ convolution without padding loses $2$ from the side; $2\times2$ pooling halves it. Input $572$ (the original, [Added]).

p07-sizes-down-wrap-t.name: p07-sizes-down-wrap-t
p07-sizes-down-wrap-t.text:
The bottom is $28\times28$ ($32$ after pooling, $28$ after two convolutions).
The sides of each level of the contracting path 'after two convolutions' are $568,\ 280,\ 136,\ 64$ — these four numbers are the left feature maps the right side must align with.

p08-crop-title.name: p08-crop-title
p08-crop-title.text: The left is larger than the right: what to do before the skip? Crop

p08-crop-ctx.name: p08-crop-ctx
p08-crop-ctx.text: The side after enlarging in the expansive path does not match the left: the left is larger, so the left map must first be cropped by a margin on every side before concatenation.

p08-crop-out-t.name: p08-crop-out-t
p08-crop-out-t.text: The final output is $388\times388$, smaller than the input $572\times572$.

p08-crop-mod-t.name: p08-crop-mod-t
p08-crop-mod-t.text: Modern implementations use padding $1$: the size stays unchanged, left and right of the same level are equal from the start, no cropping is needed, and the output is as large as the input. Example: input $256$: $256\to128\to64\to32\to16$, then enlarged back $32\to64\to128\to256$ [Added].

p08-crop-ex-t.name: p08-crop-ex-t
p08-crop-ex-t.text: Common error: thinking the output of U-Net is always as large as the input.

p09-practice-b-q1-t.name: p09-practice-b-q1-t
p09-practice-b-q1-t.text: Input $572$ passes two unpadded $3\times3$ convolutions and then a $2\times2$ pooling with stride $2$: what are the sides in turn?

p09-practice-b-q2-t.name: p09-practice-b-q2-t
p09-practice-b-q2-t.text: After enlarging, a level of the expansive path is $104$ and the matching feature map on the left is $136$. How much is cropped per side?

p09-practice-b-a2-t.name: p09-practice-b-a2-t
p09-practice-b-a2-t.text: The left is larger than the right by $136-104=32$; cropping equally on both sides, each side loses $32/2=16$. After cropping the left is also $104$ and can be concatenated with the right.

p10-loss-title.name: p10-loss-title
p10-loss-title.text: One cross-entropy for each pixel, then the mean

p10-loss-ctx.name: p10-loss-ctx
p10-loss-ctx.text: The last feature map has $c$ channels (one per class), followed by softmax, so each pixel gets probabilities adding up to $1$. The loss is the per-pixel $-\log\mathbb{P}_p$, then averaged.

p10-loss-worst-t.name: p10-loss-worst-t
p10-loss-worst-t.text: The pixel with probability $0.2$ is the most wrong and has the largest loss. Segmentation is per-pixel classification, and the loss is again cross-entropy.

p11-practice-c-title.name: p11-practice-c-title
p11-practice-c-title.text: Your turn: the mean loss of three pixels

p11-practice-c-q-t.name: p11-practice-c-q-t
p11-practice-c-q-t.text: The true-class probabilities of three pixels are $0.5,\ 0.5,\ 0.25$. What is the mean cross-entropy loss?

p12-training-title.name: p12-training-title
p12-training-title.text: How was the original trained? How large is it?

p12-training-ctx.name: p12-training-ctx
p12-training-ctx.text: The original was trained in Caffe. Biomedical image tiles are large, so the batch size is only $1$.

p12-training-mo-h.name: p12-training-mo-h
p12-training-mo-h.text: Momentum: the source and the original paper differ

p12-training-mo-t.name: p12-training-mo-t
p12-training-mo-t.text: The source says momentum $0.9$, the same as VGG; but the original U-Net paper says $0.99$ [Added]. Here the original paper is followed as a reminder to the reader.

p12-training-wm-t.name: p12-training-wm-t
p12-training-wm-t.text: The original loss also adds a boundary weight map so that the thin gaps between neighbouring cells count more [Added]; this unit covers only per-pixel cross-entropy.

p12-training-wn.name: p12-training-wn
p12-training-wn.text: Number of weights (biases not counted): channels 64→1024, 1 input channel, 2 output classes [Added]

p12-training-lt-t.name: p12-training-lt-t
p12-training-lt-t.text: Much smaller: U-Net has no huge fully connected layer, only convolutions.

p13-misconceptions-title.name: p13-misconceptions-title
p13-misconceptions-title.text: What is wrong with these four statements?

p13-misconceptions-ctx.name: p13-misconceptions-ctx
p13-misconceptions-ctx.text: Judge each one first, then read the correction on the right.

p13-misconceptions-m0-t.name: p13-misconceptions-m0-t
p13-misconceptions-m0-t.text: 'A transposed convolution can restore what pooling discarded.'

p13-misconceptions-c0-t.name: p13-misconceptions-c0-t
p13-misconceptions-c0-t.text: It only enlarges the size; the details are restored by skip connections.

p13-misconceptions-m1-t.name: p13-misconceptions-m1-t
p13-misconceptions-m1-t.text: 'The output of U-Net is always as large as the input.'

p13-misconceptions-c2-t.name: p13-misconceptions-c2-t
p13-misconceptions-c2-t.text: It came from medical segmentation, but its structure (contract, expand, skip) works for any task with per-pixel output.

p13-misconceptions-m3-t.name: p13-misconceptions-m3-t
p13-misconceptions-m3-t.text: 'The loss for segmentation differs from classification.'

p13-misconceptions-c3-t.name: p13-misconceptions-c3-t
p13-misconceptions-c3-t.text: Both are cross-entropy, only computed per pixel and averaged.

p14-quiz-a-ctx.name: p14-quiz-a-ctx
p14-quiz-a-ctx.text: The source's questions with all options; the source page marks no answers, so the answers and explanations are written from this unit ([Added]).

p14-quiz-a-q0-t.name: p14-quiz-a-q0-t
p14-quiz-a-q0-t.text:
What is the division of labour between the contracting path and the expansive path of U-Net?
A. Both only classify and do no localization
B. The contracting path catches context and the expansive path localizes precisely
C. The contracting path does only fully connected layers and the expansive path only LRN
D. The two have identical functions and are drawn as a U just to look nice

p14-quiz-a-a0-t.name: p14-quiz-a-a0-t
p14-quiz-a-a0-t.text: Answer B. The contracting path shrinks and catches context, the expansive path enlarges and localizes (Section 1).

p14-quiz-a-q1-t.name: p14-quiz-a-q1-t
p14-quiz-a-q1-t.text:
Why must the original U-Net crop before a skip connection?
A. Because unpadded convolutions shrink the feature maps step by step and the two sides do not match in size
B. Because softmax changes the spatial size
C. Because the stride of max pooling must be 3
D. Because the number of output channels must be 1000

p14-quiz-a-a1-t.name: p14-quiz-a-a1-t
p14-quiz-a-a1-t.text: Answer A. Without padding each convolution loses two cells, the left map is larger than the right, so it must be cropped first (Section 4).

p15-quiz-b-ctx.name: p15-quiz-b-ctx
p15-quiz-b-ctx.text: The source's questions with all options; the source page marks no answers, so the answers and explanations are written from this unit ([Added]).

p15-quiz-b-q0-t.name: p15-quiz-b-q0-t
p15-quiz-b-q0-t.text:
Which operation does the expansive path of U-Net use to enlarge feature maps?
A. Another max pooling with stride 2
B. $2\times2$ deconvolution / transposed convolution
C. Copying the image four times
D. Only $1\times1$ convolution to raise the spatial resolution

p15-quiz-b-a0-t.name: p15-quiz-b-a0-t
p15-quiz-b-a0-t.text: Answer B. The expansive path enlarges with a 2×2 transposed convolution (Section 3). A shrinks; C and D are not how it is done.

p15-quiz-b-q1-t.name: p15-quiz-b-q1-t
p15-quiz-b-q1-t.text:
What was U-Net's original main application and output form?
A. 10-class handwritten digit classification, with a 10-dimensional vector output
B. Biomedical image segmentation; output of the same spatial size as the input, $c$ class channels + softmax + cross-entropy
C. Machine translation
D. Only super-resolution, with no class channels

p15-quiz-b-a1-t.name: p15-quiz-b-a1-t
p15-quiz-b-a1-t.text: Answer B. Biomedical image segmentation, with c class channels, softmax and per-pixel cross-entropy (Section 5). 'The same spatial size' holds for the padded version; the original unpadded version is slightly smaller.

p16-summary-title.name: p16-summary-title
p16-summary-title.text: One sentence, plain words, formulas: what to take away from KP05

p16-summary-ctx.name: p16-summary-ctx
p16-summary-ctx.text: Close the slides and try to say the one-sentence version yourself.

p16-summary-one-t.name: p16-summary-one-t
p16-summary-one-t.text: U-Net catches context with the contracting path (two $3\times3$ convolutions, $2\times2$ pooling, channels doubled), localizes precisely with the expansive path ($2\times2$ transposed convolution, channels halved, concatenation with the same-level left features, two $3\times3$ convolutions), outputs the class probabilities of every pixel and is trained with per-pixel cross-entropy.

p16-summary-plain-t.name: p16-summary-plain-t
p16-summary-plain-t.text: Like first shrinking a map to see the whole (this is the city centre) and then enlarging it step by step back to the original scale; when enlarging, the clear street outlines of the original map are pasted back so it does not blur into a mess.

p16-summary-fix-h.name: p16-summary-fix-h
p16-summary-fix-h.text: Corrections and choices relative to the source

p16-summary-fix-t.name: p16-summary-fix-t
p16-summary-fix-t.text:
1. The source says no padding and also that the output has the same size as the input, which contradict each other: without padding it is $572\to388$.
2. Momentum: source $0.9$, original paper $0.99$.
3. Channels, the size chain and the total number of weights are [Added].

p16-summary-next-h.name: p16-summary-next-h
p16-summary-next-h.text: The question for the next unit

p16-summary-next-t.name: p16-summary-next-t
p16-summary-next-t.text:
Is a deeper network always better? Empirically, beyond about $20$ layers, adding depth makes the training accuracy saturate first and then worsen.
The next unit (KP06) looks at how ResNet solves this degradation problem.

p01-hook-nav.name: p01-hook-nav
p01-hook-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP05 · 01/16 · §1 Start · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p01-hook-cue0.name: p01-hook-cue0
p01-hook-cue0.text: Recall first: the networks of the previous three units take the whole image in and output one class.

p01-hook-cue1.name: p01-hook-cue1
p01-hook-cue1.text: Segmentation: label every pixel of the image; the output is a 'label map' as large as the input.

p01-hook-cue2.name: p01-hook-cue2
p01-hook-cue2.text: To output a label map of the same size, the network must first shrink to catch context and then enlarge to localize — that is U-Net.

p02-shape-nav.name: p02-shape-nav
p02-shape-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP05 · 02/16 · §1 Structure · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p02-shape-cue0.name: p02-shape-cue0
p02-shape-cue0.text: First the left half: side 568→280→136→64→28, channels 64→1024, shrinking all the way to catch context.

p02-shape-cue1.name: p02-shape-cue1
p02-shape-cue1.text: Then the right half: enlarging back to 388, channels halving, in charge of precise localization.

p02-shape-cue2.name: p02-shape-cue2
p02-shape-cue2.text: Gold dashed lines: each left level sends its feature maps to the same level on the right, joining the two sides into a U.

p03-contract-nav.name: p03-contract-nav
p03-contract-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP05 · 03/16 · §2 Contracting path · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p03-contract-cue0.name: p03-contract-cue0
p03-contract-cue0.text: First: two 3×3 convolutions, each followed by ReLU.

p03-contract-cue1.name: p03-contract-cue1
p03-contract-cue1.text: Second: 2×2 max pooling with stride 2, the side is halved.

p03-contract-cue2.name: p03-contract-cue2
p03-contract-cue2.text: Third: each downsampling doubles the channels.

p03-contract-cue3.name: p03-contract-cue3
p03-contract-cue3.text: Down the path the channels are 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024.

p03-contract-cue4.name: p03-contract-cue4
p03-contract-cue4.text: The start 64 is the original's setting (the source gives none); shrinking space and deepening channels widens the view.

p04-tconv-nav.name: p04-tconv-nav
p04-tconv-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP05 · 04/16 · §3 Expansive path · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p04-tconv-cue0.name: p04-tconv-cue0
p04-tconv-cue0.text: First the input and the kernel: both 2×2.

p04-tconv-cue1.name: p04-tconv-cue1
p04-tconv-cue1.text: Input 1 times the whole kernel is written into the upper-left 2×2 block.

p04-tconv-cue2.name: p04-tconv-cue2
p04-tconv-cue2.text: Input 2 times the kernel is written into the upper right; 3 and 4 fill the lower two blocks the same way.

p04-tconv-cue3.name: p04-tconv-cue3
p04-tconv-cue3.text: The four blocks form 4×4, doubling the side; a transposed convolution only enlarges, details come back through skip connections.

p05-practice-a-nav.name: p05-practice-a-nav
p05-practice-a-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP05 · 05/16 · Practice · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p05-practice-a-cue0.name: p05-practice-a-cue0
p05-practice-a-cue0.text: Work it out yourself: the all-ones kernel, the channels after concatenation, the side with padding.

p05-practice-a-cue1.name: p05-practice-a-cue1
p05-practice-a-cue1.text: Answers: every cell enlarged into 2×2; 1024 channels; side 16.

p06-skip-nav.name: p06-skip-nav
p06-skip-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP05 · 06/16 · §3 Skip connection · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p06-skip-cue0.name: p06-skip-cue0
p06-skip-cue0.text: The same-level feature map on the left still keeps the details: where the edges are.

p06-skip-cue1.name: p06-skip-cue1
p06-skip-cue1.text: The map enlarged from below carries context but its edges are already blurred.

p06-skip-cue2.name: p06-skip-cue2
p06-skip-cue2.text: Concatenating them along the channels: details and context stacked together.

p06-skip-cue3.name: p06-skip-cue3
p06-skip-cue3.text: The following two 3×3 convolutions can use both kinds of information.

p06-skip-cue4.name: p06-skip-cue4
p06-skip-cue4.text: So a transposed convolution does not undo pooling; the details are restored by the skip connection.

p07-sizes-down-nav.name: p07-sizes-down-nav
p07-sizes-down-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP05 · 07/16 · §4 Sizes (down) · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p07-sizes-down-cue0.name: p07-sizes-down-cue0
p07-sizes-down-cue0.text: Input 572: two convolutions each lose 2, giving 570, 568; pooling halves to 284.

p07-sizes-down-cue4.name: p07-sizes-down-cue4
p07-sizes-down-cue4.text: Reaching the bottom: 30, 28. The sides of the four left levels after two convolutions are 568, 280, 136, 64.

p08-crop-nav.name: p08-crop-nav
p08-crop-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP05 · 08/16 · §4 Sizes (up) and cropping · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p08-crop-cue0.name: p08-crop-cue0
p08-crop-cue0.text: First the lowest level (level 4): left 64, right 56 after enlarging, crop 4 per side, then two convolutions give 52.

p08-crop-cue1.name: p08-crop-cue1
p08-crop-cue1.text: Level 3: 136 versus 104, crop 16 per side, giving 100.

p08-crop-cue2.name: p08-crop-cue2
p08-crop-cue2.text: Level 2: 280 versus 200, crop 40 per side, giving 196.

p08-crop-cue3.name: p08-crop-cue3
p08-crop-cue3.text: Top level: 568 versus 392, crop 88 per side, giving 388.

p08-crop-cue4.name: p08-crop-cue4
p08-crop-cue4.text: So the original U-Net outputs 388×388, smaller than the input 572: the price of no padding.

p08-crop-cue5.name: p08-crop-cue5
p08-crop-cue5.text: Modern implementations use padding, need no cropping, and the output is as large as the input.

p09-practice-b-nav.name: p09-practice-b-nav
p09-practice-b-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP05 · 09/16 · Practice · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p09-practice-b-cue0.name: p09-practice-b-cue0
p09-practice-b-cue0.text: Work it out yourself: the sides after convolution and pooling, how much to crop per side.

p10-loss-nav.name: p10-loss-nav
p10-loss-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP05 · 10/16 · §5 Output and loss · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p10-loss-cue0.name: p10-loss-cue0
p10-loss-cue0.text: A 2×2 image whose four pixels have true-class probabilities 0.7, 0.5, 0.9, 0.2.
